Vision and Values
Vision statement
‘Intelligence plus Character - that is the goal of true education’ Martin Luther King Jr.
At Springwest, we are determined that each and every student achieves and flourishes. Therefore, we strive to teach ‘Great lessons - every period, every day’ to ensure that our students gain a breadth of knowledge, develop curiosity about the world around them and are equipped to make good moral choices.
Values
Believe
We believe in our students, our staff, our school and our local community. We recognise that all students are unique and have different interests and talents. Our high expectations for all, excellent pastoral care and focus on character development ensure that every student feels valued and able to succeed.
Belong
Our culture of kindness promotes a strong sense of belonging for our staff and students. We are proud to be part of the Springwest community. Our huge range of extra-curricular activities, leadership opportunities, houses, educational trips and visits and a strong prioritisation of sports and the arts ensure that all students can develop their passions and shine.
Flourish
Our ultimate aim for students is eudaimonia- living a life that is both morally good and happy. We want to equip them with character virtues and phronesis (the wisdom to determine the best moral action) so that they can make a positive contribution to Springwest and society.
Virtues
Our Character Education framework, based on research from the Jubilee Centre at the University of Birmingham, focuses on the development of four virtue groups: Intellectual, Moral, Civic and Performance.
Intellectual Virtues
Our students are given many opportunities to develop ambition, curiosity and autonomy within and outside of lessons.
Civic Virtues
Our students are encouraged to volunteer, be charitable and develop community pride.
Moral Virtues
Our students are expected to forgive others, show empathy and express gratitude. In our designated ‘Reflection Weeks’ all students write gratitude slips to families and staff.
Performance Virtues
Our students can attend a range of co-curricular clubs each week and try new activities on Character Days. The Performance Virtues of collaboration, bravery and creativity are consistently modelled by staff and promoted through lessons and beyond.
Logo and Motto
Our logo reflects our school history, vision and values. Our motto 'Benignitas Prima' emphasises the importance of kindness in all our actions. We encourage both staff and students to consistently embody this value in their interactions with one another within school and within our wider community.

Principal's Welcome
'Intelligence plus Character, that is the goal of true education' - Martin Luther King Jr.
I am extremely proud to be the Principal of Springwest Academy, a vibrant, mixed comprehensive school serving the local community of Feltham. Having been in post since September 2020 it has been a pleasure to witness how Springwest has developed and improved. My personal priorities - a culture of kindness, strong academic outcomes and excellent behaviour - have inspired positive changes in both our outcomes, where we achieved our best ever results this summer, and our culture. As a 'Regional Character Hub' school we have developed a strong sense of belonging, where students and staff flourish.
We pride ourselves on providing an ambitious, rigorous, knowledge-rich curriculum and introduce students to challenging and thought-provoking content from the start of Year 7. In addition to knowledge, we see ‘understanding’ and ‘memory’ to be at the heart of learning and therefore students are given opportunities for extended writing, discussions and retrieval practice within all of their subjects. At Springwest we have also developed Prep sessions which allow students to start the day in a purposeful manner by either reading, using their knowledge organisers to complete their homework, or attending PE Prep, where our teams have extra time to train together.
Our values of ‘Believe’, ‘Belong’ and ‘Flourish’ are embodied in all that we do. These values are complemented by our Character Framework which develops the four virtue groups: Moral, Intellectual, Civic and Performance. We provide students with many opportunities to develop their characters through explicit Character Education lessons at KS3, a wide range of extra-curricular activities, opportunities on Character Days and our Springwest Baccalaureate.
We stretch and challenge the more able and have developed our Scholars’ Programme to inspire ambition and broaden knowledge beyond the curriculum. Student Leadership is integral to our school community and culture. In addition to our Head Students and Prefects, we have Heads of House, a Student Council, Creative Arts Specialists, Sports Leaders, an Eco-Committee, Anti-Bullying Ambassadors and Library Monitors. Students at all levels of leadership are invited to join the ‘Leadership Academy’ an initiative run by our SLT which develops moral leadership skills and empowers students to become effective leaders.
We are an inclusive school and have a strong pastoral support system, including a designated member of the Senior Leadership Team, Head of Year and Pastoral Mentor for each year group. Students with SEND or EAL are well supported by specialist teachers within mainstream lessons and smaller numeracy and literacy groups. In addition, we have two Local Authority resourced Centres which provide provision for students with physical disabilities and Autism.
We are fortunate to have beautiful outdoor spaces which include both raised and sunken gardens as well as playing fields, two astro pitches and a MUGA. Our outstanding facilities are regularly used by the local community at evenings and weekends.
I would encourage you to have a look at the video below and contact us if you would like to visit.

Performing Arts (Dance, Drama & Music)
"The Arts, it has said, cannot change the world, but they may change human beings who might change the world" - Maxine Greene
Performing Arts Is...
Performing Arts is a creative education developed through Creation, Performance, Analysis and Evaluative skills. Students have three Performing Arts lessons each week during their time as a KS3 student at Springwest Academy where they study a range of disciplines including Drama, Dance, Music, Technical Theatre, The Performing Arts Business & Theatre Journalism. Students can also undertake a Performing Arts subject at KS4 and/or can also get involved in one of the many clubs, productions or opportunities we offer as part of our Co-Curricular offer. The Performing Arts curriculum will allow students to develop a lifelong appreciation of The Arts.
Sequence of Learning
Dance - World of Dance Drama - Darkwood Manor Music - Singing, fundamentals of musical elements and exploring folk music
Dance - Dance Techniques (Street Dance & Musical Theatre) Drama - Blood Brothers Music - Keyboard Skills and musical elements
Dance - Contemporary Explorations Drama - Theatre in Education Music - Music in the movies and composition
Dance - The Aspire Project
Dance - Exploring the Performing Arts
Dance - Developing Skills and Techniques in the Performing Arts
Drama - Eduqas Level 1/2 Vocational Award in Performing Arts Technical Award Units 1 & 2
Music - Pearson BTEC Level 1/Level 2 Tech Award in Music Practice
Dance -Component 3 - Responding to a Brief
Drama - Eduqas Level 1/2 Vocational Award in Performing Arts Technical Award Unit 3

pageCache.text:
News
Year 11 Geography Rivers Trip to Epping Forest
All Year 11 Geography students recently visited Epping Forest on a bright, sunny day to complete essential fieldwork for their Paper 3 exam. While investigating the river characteristics of Debden Brook, the cohort enthusiastically waded into the water to measure width, depth and velocity across three distinct sites.
The trip was a resounding success, leaving students thoroughly engaged, full of hands-on experience and exceptionally well prepared for their upcoming assessments.

pageCache.pageTitle: KS3 Pupils Impress in Social Enterprise Challenge - News - Springwest Academy
pageCache.text:
News
KS3 Pupils Impress in Social Enterprise Challenge
KS3 pupils at Springwest Academy recently took part in a Dragon's Den-style social enterprise challenge, where students developed business ideas aimed at supporting their community.
Pupils showed excellent creativity, confidence and teamwork as they presented their ideas to a panel of judges. One team, Springwest Saves, was awarded the Best Teamwork prize for their community-focused food enterprise using homemade jams and chutneys to reduce waste and support local food banks.
The judges praised the team's focus on sustainability, use of school-grown produce and positive community impact. They also encouraged pupils to continue developing the project through branding, packaging and a future tea party launch event.
Springwest Academy is incredibly proud of all pupils involved and the enthusiasm and professionalism they showed throughout the project.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 8 Reward Trip to Kew Gardens - News - Springwest Academy
pageCache.text:
News
Year 8 Reward Trip to Kew Gardens
A group of Year 8 students enjoyed a reward trip to Kew Gardens to celebrate their hard work and enthusiasm in Geography. The visit was linked to their recent learning on tropical rainforests, giving students the opportunity to experience many of the plants and environments they had studied in the classroom. During the day, students took part in an engaging educational workshop, where they explored the importance of tropical rainforests, their uses, their biodiversity and the need to protect these vital ecosystems.
When asked to reflect on the trip this is what some students had to say:
"I loved when we saw the two glasshouses, the Temperate and the Tropical. Although my favourite part of the trip was when we got to relax in nature. It was very hot that day but when we relaxed in the shade, the breeze cooled me down a lot. I also loved when we were very high up on the treetop walk. Not only could we see nature, but we also saw parts of the City of London" Alexis S
"On the Kew Gardens trip we saw many plants. An example was giant bamboo. This is a type of grass. Also, the giant bamboo can grow extremely fast in about 16 days. This was found in the Tropical House. The climate was extremely humid, just like the environment in the rainforest" Rianne R
Despite the hot weather, students made the most of the sunshine and represented the school brilliantly throughout the visit. It was a fantastic day of learning beyond the classroom and a well-deserved reward for their hard work and positive attitude.

pageCache.pageTitle: Springwest Academy Achieves AI in Education Explorer Level - News - Springwest Academy
pageCache.text:
News
Springwest Academy Achieves AI in Education Explorer Level
We are delighted to announce that Springwest Academy has achieved Explorer Level in the AI in Education (AiEd) Certified Framework.
This recognition celebrates our commitment to the responsible, ethical and purposeful use of AI in education. The Explorer Level acknowledges the work we have undertaken to build understanding, identify opportunities and begin developing appropriate AI practice across our school community.
This is an exciting milestone in our AI journey and reflects our commitment to exploring innovative approaches that can enhance teaching, learning and the wider experience of our students.
We look forward to building on this strong foundation as we continue to develop our use of AI at Springwest Academy.
Congratulations to everyone involved!

Thank you for your continued support and congratulations to the incredible Class of 2026 on their historic, record-breaking success.
We are exceptionally proud of them.

We are delighted that our students can now enjoy brand-new, state-of-the-art changing facilities.
Sports influencer and presenter Jemel One Five joined us to officially open the new facility, which represents an investment close to half a million pounds and includes new changing rooms, showers, sinks and toilets.
The facilities are used throughout the school week by Springwest Academy students and will provide a much-improved environment for PE and sport.

Careers Guidance
What is CEIAG?
CEIAG (Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance) provides students with knowledge and understanding about their next steps after Springwest. We aim to build our students' ambition and confidence to enable them to make informed choices about their future education and employment.
Our weekly PSHE lessons, alongside our Character Education Curriculum at KS3, ensure that our students develop holistically. Therefore, they leave us with the employability and study skills needed to be successful in the world of work.
Our CEIAG lead is: Ms Hopson
Email: c.hopson@springwestacademy.org
Information for parents
Information for Students and TeachersGatsby Benchmarks
Our Careers Programme is developed from the Gatsby Benchmarks and the Career Development Institutes’ ‘Framework for careers, employability and enterprise education’.
The eight Gatsby Benchmarks are:
A stable careers programme
Learning from career and labour market information
Addressing the needs of each pupil
Linking curriculum learning to careers
Encounters with employers and employees
Experiences of workplaces
Encounters with further and higher education
Personal guidance
How is CEIAG Implemented at Springwest?
Students are introduced to our Springwest Virtues through our Character Curriculum. In both their Character lessons and on Character Days, they have opportunities to develop and reflect on these virtues.
Students develop their critical thinking and communication skills through their Character lessons which are underpinned by the Trivium. They also begin to think about what their interests are and the skills and qualities they might need when they leave school through Unifrog. From Year 8, students are able to be part of our collaboration with Aim Higher.
Students work with local charities through the First Give Programme. They complete research into the charity's vision, operations and marketing; allowing them to see first hand how a company operates.
The focus on Character Days is CEIAG. During these days, students will hear from local colleges, sixth forms and universities. They will also complete skills tests and reflect on their results, investigate different careers and begin writing college/ sixth form/ job personal statements. All Year 10 students have a mock interview with an external professional and receive feedback.
In addition, we provide talks and assemblies for students on apprenticeships, local labour market information and different options for post-16.
All of our Year 10 students complete work experience in the summer term, allowing them to gain valuable real life experience. Last year's placements included: shadowing an MP in Parliament, working with an electrician, working at MRM communication solutions, working at media company UM London and working at local nurseries and primary schools. Placements are logged via Unifrog.
WEX Letter Unifrog - Placement Guide Unifrog - Adding a placement guide
Our Year 11 students receive more personalised careers advice from our Innervate Careers Advisor. who meets students one on one. We also provide information to families through our Year 11 Post-16 Information Evening. All Year 11 students are supported to apply for their next steps by their HOY, tutors and subject teachers. They also have the opportunity to attend a careers fair in the autumn term.
